quiz.question: Why compare the complete source count?

choices.text: A larger value can share the same low 32 bits.
Every source has a variable number of pixels.
The destination must be sixteen-byte aligned.

hints.text: Counts are byte quantities in full-width registers.
Reject count and native alignment before context loads.

quiz.question: What must the output capacity include?

choices.text: Only the 12,288 RGB bytes.
The sixteen-byte header and all RGB payload bytes.
The native previous image as well as the record.

hints.text: The record count includes its header.
Admit every writable window before reading pixel values.

quiz.question: Which sequence belongs in the new record header?

choices.text: The already incremented next-sequence value.
The source byte count.
The input next-sequence value.

hints.text: The header identifies the record being produced now.
Advance sequence only after the record and previous image are complete.

quiz.question: Why validate the last color before emitting the first triple?

choices.text: A late invalid color must leave the entire output unchanged.
The CRC cannot process zero bytes.
RGB order depends on the last pixel.

hints.text: A full-source validation pass establishes the later output pass can complete.
The source word has 24 color bits and eight required zero bits.

quiz.question: Which byte sequence represents sequence 255 on the wire?

choices.text: 00 FF 00 FF.

hints.text: Record integers are big-endian in both simulator byte orders.
Use byte stores so the record needs no native alignment.

quiz.question: What does the header length field count?

choices.text: The entire record including its header.
The destination allocation.
Payload bytes only.

hints.text: Distinguish the wire payload length from the callable return count.
Twelve thousand two hundred eighty-eight is hexadecimal 0x3000.

quiz.question: Why extract numeric channels instead of copying three memory bytes?

choices.text: Native word byte order differs from the RGB wire order.
Every color channel is a native doubleword.
All source memory bytes are already in RGB order.

hints.text: A native load recovers the same number in either target byte order.
Source and payload cursors advance by different byte strides.

quiz.question: Which bytes are excluded from the CRC input?

choices.text: The payload.
The four bytes reserved for the stored CRC itself.
The sequence field.

hints.text: The checksum input concatenates header bytes 0–11 and the payload.
Do not reset the accumulator when the feed loop changes ranges.

quiz.question: Which shift belongs in the reflected CRC update?

choices.text: A signed word right shift.
A rotation through the previous image.
A logical doubleword right shift.

hints.text: The recurrence shifts in zero, independent of bit 31.
Test the original low bit before shifting it away.

quiz.question: When should the stored checksum be included in this CRC calculation?

choices.text: Never; its field is excluded.
Before processing the payload.
After every color word.

hints.text: Finalize once after both covered ranges.
Stored byte order is a separate step from computing the numeric CRC.

quiz.question: Which image should a later delta use as its predecessor?

choices.text: The source of the most recent failed attempt.
The source of the last successfully encoded record.
An arbitrary displayed seek target.

hints.text: Prediction state belongs to committed output history.
The current full record does not need old previous-image contents.

quiz.question: What follows a successful encoding at sequence 255?

choices.text: Sequence wraps to zero automatically.
The record must be discarded because 255 cannot be encoded.
Next sequence 256, which a further call rejects.

hints.text: The last legal record index and the next-sequence state have different bounds.
A rejected retry retains actual previously produced bytes and prediction state.
